CC 2. Approve the Check and Wire Registers for June 4, 2017 â€“ June 17, 2017 in the amount of $2,596,352.63. Approve the Check Registers as presented.
At each regular City Council Meeting, the City Council is presented with the financial claims (invoices) against the City for purchase of materials, supplies, services, and capital projects for checks and Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments issued the prior two to three weeks. This process provides the City Council the opportunity to review the expenses of the City. The justifying backup information for each expenditure is available in the Finance Department.

CC 3. Adopt Ordinance No. 1028, amending Chapter 17.12 of the Lancaster Municipal Code to modify the setbacks, building orientation, and building design requirements in the C (Commercial) and OP (Office Professional) zones.
The proposed ordinance would modify the current requirements of the Cityâ€™s C (Commercial) and OP (Office Professional) zones with respect to street setbacks, building orientation, and building design. The ordinance would also have the effect of modifying the requirements of the Cityâ€™s CPD (Commercial Planned Development) zone requirements, because the CPD references to the C zone requirements as a guideline for development.

CC 4. Adopt Ordinance No. 1029, amending the Lancaster Municipal Code (Title 16) to allow approval of multi-year extension requests for tentative maps.
The proposed amendment revises Section 16.08.140 to clearly establish that both tentative parcel maps and tentative tract maps can be extended for an aggregate period not to exceed three years. There would be no limit on the length of any individual extension provided that the aggregate total did not exceed the three-year period.

The City is requesting approval of Additional Authorization No.Â 1 in an amount not to exceed $50,054.00 for additional civil design services, and for landscaping and irrigation design plans on the east side of Avenue I at 10th Street West, where a meandering sidewalk will be installed at the northeast and southeast corners and match existing landscaping at the site.
CC 5

CC 6. Award Public Works Construction Project No. 17-009, 5th Street East Corridor Improvements ATPL-5419(046), to C.A. Rasmussen, Inc., of Valencia, California, in the amount of $1,810,445.00, plus a 15% contingency, for the construction of pedestrian curb bulb-outs, traffic signal modifications, and the installation of buffered bike lanes, and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
The 5th Street East corridor, from Avenue H-8 to Avenue J-4, was selected based on the need for safety improvements for students walking or bicycling to and from school. This corridor is adjacent to three public schools: El Dorado Elementary, Linda Verde Elementary, and Piute Middle School. The proposed improvements will include the construction of pedestrian curb bulb-outs, with ADA compliant curb ramps to shorten crossing distance at several locations along 5th Street East, and new traffic striping to install buffered bike lanes. These proposed improvements are in compliance with the Master Plan of Trails and Bikeways. This project is primarily funded with Active Transportation Program (ATP) grant funds.
CC 6
CC 6 attachment
CC 7. Award Public Works Construction Project No. 16-002, Lancaster Boulevard, 30th Street to 40th Street East, to R.C. Becker and Son, Inc., of Santa Clarita, California, in the amount of $577,910.37, plus a 15% contingency, for roadway resurfacing and improvements; and authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to sign all documents. This contract is awarded to the lowest responsible bidder per California Public Code Section 22038 (b).
The project involves pavement rehabilitation, restriping, repair of existing sidewalk, and curb ramp modifications, on Lancaster Boulevard between 30th Street and 40th Street East. Work will be performed in compliance with the Cityâ€™s 2014 ADA Transition Plan, which will include reconstruction of one (1) curb ramp, installation of truncated domes on nine (9) existing curb ramps, and 185 square feet of sidewalk.
CC 7
CC 7 attachment
CC 8. Accept the work constructed by Security Paving Company, Inc., for Public Works Construction Project No. 10-011, State Route 14 and Avenue I Interchange Improvements, and direct the City Clerk to file the Notice of Completion for the project. Retention on this project has been disbursed in accordance with California Public Contract Code.
On September 13, 2011, Council awarded Public Works Construction Project No. 10-011, State Route 14 and Avenue I Interchange Improvements, to Security Paving Company, Inc. This project included widening of Avenue I to three lanes in each direction, and provided dual left-turn lanes onto State Route 14 from both the eastbound and westbound directions. The existing southbound off-ramp was removed, and a new loop ramp was constructed to intersect with Avenue I at 23rd Street West, providing a single quadrant cloverleaf interchange. The northbound State Route 14 freeway ramp configuration remained a diamond configuration with minor modifications and widening at the intersection with Avenue I. A new independent bridge structure was constructed over Avenue I adjacent to the existing southbound State Route 14 Bridge. Retaining walls were constructed beneath State Route 14 along both sides of Avenue I in order to facilitate the widening. Existing overhead Edison utilities were moved underground. Drainage improvements consisting of a new mainline within Avenue I, from 23rd Street West to Amargosa Creek, with new catch basins and laterals, were constructed to facilitate the southbound off-ramp and the widening of Avenue I. Construction of the project has been completed to the satisfaction of the Development Services Director.

NB 2
NB 2 attachment
Sawyer Construction & Associates ranked No. 1 at the end of the evaluation and selection process. Based on this ranking, on January 24, 2017, the City Council approved and authorized the award of a professional services agreement for the Design Phase of this project. Therefore staff recommends the award of the Build Phase to Sawyer Construction & Associates of Mojave, California.
NB 3. Approval of Energy Efficiency Program Plan for Submittal to California Public Utilities Commission for Administration Energy Efficiency Programs
Recommendation:
Approve Energy Efficiency Program Plan for submittal to the California Public Utilities Commission requesting funding for administration of energy efficiency programs.
NB 3
NB 3 attachment
Now in its second year of operation, LCE desires to offer energy efficiency programs that can serve customers better and timelier than existing options through SCE. LCE is electing to become an administer of ratepayer funds, collected from electric service customers through a non-bypassable charge authorized by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), for energy efficiency and conservation programs. To become an administrator, LCE must submit a plan, approved by its governing board, to the commission for the administration of cost-effective energy efficiency and conservation programs for its customers which includes funding requirements, program description, a cost-effective analysis, and the duration of the program.
